result:
Design pre-registered to `runs/pending_experiment.json`. Here's the experiment:

**Experiment 2 — Classify-then-refine coordinate parameterization** (category: architecture, from-scratch init)

**Read of the history:** the lineage on this branch has exactly one row — the eval-v2 baseline seed at 1993.71 m worst-case median. That error is ~29% of Berlin's 6.9 km map extent, which is the classic signature of MSE regression-to-the-mean: a single sigmoid (u,v) head averaged over a multimodal answer space gets dragged toward the map centroid whenever features are ambiguous. So the first real experiment attacks the output parameterization, not capacity or training scale — the strongest single lever, and explicitly a "strong experiment" family per the design rules. (The library's only entry, night-frame denoising, doesn't apply on this daytime-only branch.)

**The one change:** replace the direct-regression head with a 32×32 map-cell softmax (1024 cells of ~217 m, defined in normalized coordinates so nothing is Berlin-hardcoded) plus a tanh-bounded within-cell offset regressor — PlaNet-style geo-cell classification with CenterNet-style offset refinement. Cross-entropy can't hedge between distant hypotheses the way MSE does. The conv trunk, the loose-BCE confidence mechanism (which keeps the model scoreable against the 0.3 abstention threshold), the training data budget, and the CLI/ONNX contracts all stay fixed, so the parameterization is the isolated variable. The decode (argmax cell + gathered offset) lives inside the exported ONNX graph, preserving the frozen `[[u, v, conf]]` contract.

**Prediction, pre-registered:** worst-case median drops from 1993.71 m into the 300–700 m range if top-1 cell accuracy clears ~50% — cell-scale error instead of centroid-scale. Not expected to hit the 100 m milestone alone; it removes the structural error so later work has something to refine. Refutation signature: a score still near ~2000 m would mean trunk capacity, not parameterization, is binding. Model stays ~500k params ≈ 2 MB (gate is 4 MiB), training cost essentially unchanged, so the round's wall-time is safe.

The implementation brief spells out the exact head/loss/decode edits to `model/model.py`, the one-line change to `model/train.py`, an ONNX-tracing fallback (one-hot matmul if gather-after-argmax fails to export), and restates the frozen CLI and export contracts. The harness takes it from here.
